text:
maria: Observed short-request regression after yesterday's kernel/token-budget change. Short sequences (<=64 tokens) p50 jumped from ~12ms to ~120ms; p95 ~320ms. Long sequences unchanged. Full perf link: https://dash.redwood/boards/batching?run=2026-03-16

albert: Repro steps? Which queue policy did we ship exactly?

devon: We bumped continuous_batcher.token_budget default 1024 -> 4096 in that deploy. That encourages filling batches with long requests.

maria: Right — with token_budget=4096 the batcher greedily accumulates until budget exhausted, so short requests sit in front of the queue but never get batched quickly.

sasha: Also seeing KV cache churn: long streams push past the kv window causing more cache evictions and worse latencies for followups.

tess: Quick idea: add a small_request fast-path (max_batch_tokens=256, prefer_short=true) + per-tenant token_budget caps. Keeps short latencies low while not starving bulk.

albert: So two priority buckets: fast (short seqs) and bulk (long seqs). Fast gets reserved slots or a soft quota that preempts forming batches.

devon: Prototyped preemption: if head-of-queue request length <=64, allow it to cut into the forming batch when current_batch_tokens > 2x head_tokens. That reduced wait times in local tests.

maria: Perf run (30m mixed tenants): baseline p50 short=120ms -> with preemption p50=16ms, p95=45ms. Bulk throughput dropped ~4% but overall user-facing SLOs improved.

sasha: Kernel selection note: small-batch kernel has lower setup overhead. Make sure we route to it when batch token_count < 256; otherwise switching kernels can cost more than waiting.

tess: Also added tenant fairness via token_buckets: token_budget_per_tenant = min(global_budget/num_active_tenants, tenant_weight*global_budget). Example config snippet we tested:
```
queue_policy: {
  "global_token_budget": 4096,
  "fast_max_batch_tokens": 256,
  "preempt_threshold": 2.0,
  "tenant_weights": {"prod": 2, "staging": 1, "experimental": 0.5}
}
```

albert: Two operational checks: (1) surface wait_time_by_length_bucket metric so starvation doesn't hide in avg latency, (2) monitor kv_cache_hit_rate per tenant because token caps change eviction patterns.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout to cluster-inference-phi scheduled for 2026-03-17 10:00 UTC.

devon: Running 4h canary (mixed workload). Collecting p50/p95, kv_hit, batch_kernel_switches, tenant_wait_time histograms. If canary is green we'll promote with 1hr rollback window.

maria: Can someone add a tiny repro script? Loadgen that sends ~90% short (<=32) and 10% long (>1024) across tenants. Post link here when done.

sasha: I'll add a Jenkins job and push the loadgen. Will link in this thread when it's up.

tess: TL;DR: preemptive small-batch fast-path + tenant token buckets + kernel-aware routing fixes short-sequence starvation. Need canary + new dashboard panels (wait_by_length, kv_hit_by_tenant, kernel_switch_rate). :thumbsup:
